input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Two gaps against the preferred position justify a small redline rather than a clean compliant call. (1) Duration: 19.2 gives every Deliverable only ninety days, spelled out in words. Our preferred position is 12 months for software and 90 days for services, so software Deliverables are short by nine months. Restating the period as "twelve (12) months" for software Deliverables and "ninety (90) days" for all other Deliverables both closes that gap and states the period in numerals/months, removing the ambiguity that caused the period check to fail. Hosted Services already conform throughout the subscription term (twelve-month renewals under 8.2 inside a three-year master term), which we have left untouched. (2) Remedy: 19.4 refunds only "Fees paid for it", and "Fees" is defined in 1.5 as the Implementation Fee alone. As drafted the refund backstop therefore cannot reach subscription or service charges, which materially hollows out the repair/replace/refund remedy the playbook requires; we have tied the refund to all amounts paid for the non-conforming item instead, and offered broadening the 1.5 definition as an alternative. The rest of Section 19 is compliant and unchanged: 19.1 professional and workmanlike plus conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.3 Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution, open-source protection; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace at no charge, non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies, so it does not swallow the express warranty. Fallback if Vendor resists: retain 90 days for all Deliverables provided the refund fix is accepted.

proposal.summary: Express the Deliverable conformance period numerically, extend it to 12 months for software Deliverables, and untie the warranty refund from the narrowly defined "Fees" (Implementation Fee only).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have expressed the conformance period in numerals and set it at twelve (12) months for software Deliverables (ninety (90) days for all other Deliverables), consistent with our standard 12-month software / 90-day services warranty. We have also clarified that the warranty refund covers all amounts paid for the non-conforming item, because "Fees" is defined in Section 1.5 as the Implementation Fee only, which would leave subscription and service charges unrefundable; if you prefer, we can instead broaden the Section 1.5 definition.

ops.oldText: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.
ops.newText: For twelve (12) months after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, in the case of software Deliverables, and for ninety (90) days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, in the case of all other Deliverables, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.

ops.oldText: receive a refund of Fees paid for it
ops.newText: receive a refund of all amounts paid for it (and not only the Implementation Fee)
